tasks.name: Migration 020: FTS5 Tables + Backfill
tasks.description:
Create a new migration file at `apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations/020_ConversationFTS.ts` that creates two FTS5 virtual tables and backfills them from existing projection data.

The migration should:
1. Create `projection_messages_fts` using FTS5:
   ```sql
   CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS projection_messages_fts USING fts5(
     thread_id UNINDEXED,
     message_id UNINDEXED,
     role UNINDEXED,
     message_text,
     content='projection_thread_messages',
     content_rowid='rowid'
   );
   ```
2. Create `projection_threads_fts` using FTS5:
   ```sql
   CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS projection_threads_fts USING fts5(
     thread_id UNINDEXED,
     title,
     content='projection_threads',
     content_rowid='rowid'
   );
   ```
3. Backfill messages FTS from existing data:
   ```sql
   INSERT INTO projection_messages_fts(rowid, thread_id, message_id, role, message_text)
     SELECT rowid, thread_id, message_id, role, text FROM projection_thread_messages;
   ```
4. Backfill threads FTS from existing data:
   ```sql
   INSERT INTO projection_threads_fts(rowid, thread_id, title)
     SELECT rowid, thread_id, title FROM projection_threads WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
   ```

Follow the exact migration pattern from existing migrations (e.g., `018_ProjectionThreadsArchivedAtIndex.ts`): export a default `Effect.gen()` that yields `SqlClient.SqlClient` and executes raw SQL.

Then register the migration in `apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations.ts`:
- Add import: `import Migration0020 from "./Migrations/020_ConversationFTS.ts";`
- Add entry to `migrationEntries`: `[20, "ConversationFTS", Migration0020]` (note: skip 19, it's reserved for fork schema per plan)

Note: Migration 019 is intentionally skipped (reserved). The entry array should go from `[18, ...]` to `[20, ...]`.

tasks.name: Composer: @Threads Mention Type + Trigger + Command Menu
tasks.description:
Add thread mention support to the composer system.

### 6a: Mention Type — Modify: `apps/web/src/composer-editor-mentions.ts`

Add a new segment type for thread mentions:

```typescript
export type ComposerPromptSegment =
  | { type: "text"; text: string }
  | { type: "mention"; path: string }
  | { type: "terminal-context"; context: TerminalContextDraft | null }
  | { type: "thread-mention"; threadId: string; threadTitle: string };
```

Update `splitPromptIntoComposerSegments` to detect `@Thread:` prefixed tokens:
- Pattern: `@Thread:<threadId>` or similar
- When detected, emit a `{ type: "thread-mention", threadId, threadTitle }` segment

### 6b: Trigger Detection — Modify: `apps/web/src/composer-logic.ts`

Extend `ComposerTriggerKind` to include `"thread-mention"`:
```typescript
export type ComposerTriggerKind = "path" | "slash-command" | "slash-model" | "thread-mention";
```

Update the trigger detection logic so that when the user types `@Threads` (case-insensitive), it opens the thread search sub-menu. The detection should work similarly to the `@` path trigger but check if the token starts with `@Threads` or `@threads`.

### 6c: Command Menu — Modify: `apps/web/src/components/chat/ComposerCommandMenu.tsx`

Add a new state/mode to the command menu for thread search:

1. When `trigger.kind === "thread-mention"`, render the thread search UI:
   - A search input at the top (pre-populated with trigger.query if any)
   - On keystroke, debounce (200ms) and call `nativeApi.orchestration.searchConversations()`
   - Display results: thread title, last activity date, snippet of matching content
   - Filter toggle: All / Active / Archived
   
2. When a thread result is selected:
   - Insert a `@Thread:<title>` chip into the composer text
   - Add a `ThreadMentionAttachment` to the message attachments

This is the most complex UI task. The thread search sub-menu should feel similar to the existing command menu items but with a live search experience.

**Implementation notes**:
- Use `useCallback` for the debounced search
- The search results should show thread title and a snippet from the matching content
- Include the filter toggle (All/Active/Archived) as tabs or a dropdown
- On selection, replace the `@Threads:query` text with a chip representation

Check existing patterns in ComposerCommandMenu.tsx for how other menu items work and follow the same approach.

tasks.name: Thread Summarizer: LLM Summary on Turn Start
tasks.description:
Create a thread summarizer service that generates LLM summaries of referenced threads and inject them into the conversation context.

### 1. New file: `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ThreadSummarizer.ts`

Create a service that:
1. Takes a threadId and loads the full message history
2. Calls the configured text-generation model with a summarization prompt
3. Returns the summary text

```typescript
import { Effect, Layer, ServiceMap } from "effect";
import type { ProjectionThreadMessage } from "../../persistence/Services/ProjectionThreadMessages.ts";
import { ProjectionThreadMessageRepository } from "../../persistence/Services/ProjectionThreadMessages.ts";
import { ProjectionThreadRepository } from "../../persistence/Services/ProjectionThreads.ts";

export interface ThreadSummarizerShape {
  readonly summarizeThread: (input: {
    threadId: string;
    threadTitle: string;
  }) => Effect.Effect<string, Error>;
}

export class ThreadSummarizer extends ServiceMap.Service<
  ThreadSummarizer,
  ThreadSummarizerShape
>()("t3/orchestration/ThreadSummarizer") {}
```

The implementation should:
- Load all messages for the thread via `ProjectionThreadMessageRepository.listByThreadId`
- Format messages into a conversation transcript
- For now, generate a simple extractive summary (first N messages + key content) rather than calling an LLM, since LLM integration would require significant additional infrastructure (model routing, API keys, etc.)
- Return formatted summary: `"Context from thread '[title]' (created [date]):\n[summary]"`

**Pragmatic approach**: Since calling an external LLM from within the projection/command pipeline adds significant complexity (async, failure handling, model selection), implement a simpler extractive summary for v1:
- Take the first 5 user messages and first 5 assistant messages
- Truncate each to 500 chars
- Format as a condensed transcript
- This can be upgraded to LLM-powered summarization later

### 2. Modify: `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.ts` (or the ProviderCommandReactor)

Find the turn start flow — when a `thread.turn.start` command is dispatched. Before the provider processes the user's message, check for `thread-reference` attachments in the message.

For each thread-reference attachment:
1. Call `ThreadSummarizer.summarizeThread({ threadId, threadTitle })`
2. Inject the summary as a system message preceding the user's turn

The injection point should be AFTER the user message is persisted but BEFORE it's sent to the provider. Look at how `ProviderCommandReactor` or `ProviderRuntimeIngestion` processes the turn start and find the right hook point.

Alternatively, the simplest integration point may be in the provider adapter itself — when building the messages array for the API call, detect thread-reference attachments and prepend summary context.

**Note**: This is a complex integration point. If the worker finds it too complex to inject summaries into the turn flow, a simpler approach is acceptable for v1:
- Generate the summary
- Dispatch an additional `thread.message-sent` event with role `system` containing the summary text
- This appears as a system message in the conversation before the user's message

Provide the ThreadSummarizer layer in the server layers composition.
acceptance_criteria: ThreadSummarizer service interface is defined
ThreadSummarizer layer implementation loads thread messages and generates extractive summary
Summary format is: Context from thread '[title]' (created [date]):\n[summary content]
Summary truncates appropriately for long threads (first 5 user + 5 assistant messages, 500 chars each)
ThreadSummarizer is provided in server layers
TypeScript compiles without errors

tasks.name: Agent Tool: search-conversations for Provider
tasks.description:
Register a `search-conversations` custom tool that the AI agent can call to search past conversation threads.

### Modify: Provider adapter or tool registration

Find where custom/dynamic tools are registered for the provider session. This is likely in `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts` or a related file.

Register a new tool:
```typescript
{
  name: "search-conversations",
  description: "Search past conversation threads by keyword. Use when the user asks you to find or reference previous conversations.",
  input_schema: {
    type: "object",
    properties: {
      query: { type: "string", description: "Search keywords" },
      limit: { type: "number", description: "Max results (default 5)" },
    },
    required: ["query"],
  },
}
```

Intercept in the tool execution callback:
1. Parse input (query, optional limit)
2. Call `ConversationSearchRepository.searchAll()` with the current project's projectId
3. Format results as structured text:
   ```
   Found N results across M threads:
   
   ## Thread: "<title>" (created <date>)
   - Match: <snippet>
   - Match: <snippet>
   
   ## Thread: "<title>" (created <date>)
   - Match: <snippet>
   ```
4. Return as tool result text

The tool should be:
- **Explicit only** — the agent only calls it when the user asks to search past conversations
- Classified as a `dynamic_tool_call` per existing tool patterns
- Available in all provider sessions (Claude and Codex adapters)

**Finding the right integration point**: 
- Check `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts` for how `canUseTool` or tool handlers work
- Check if there's a `tools` array or registration mechanism
- The tool needs access to `ConversationSearchRepository` and the current thread's `projectId`

If the adapter architecture makes it difficult to inject repository dependencies, consider:
- Creating a tool handler module that receives the repository as a dependency
- Or using the Effect service resolution pattern to access the repository at tool execution time

tasks.commit_message: chore: verify integration of conversation search and thread context feature

summary_context: This feature adds two tightly coupled capabilities: (1) FTS5-based full-text search across conversation threads and messages, exposed via a WS endpoint and repository layer, and (2) cross-thread context via @Threads mentions in the composer that inject summarized thread content into conversations. The search infrastructure (migration → repository → projector sync → WS endpoint → client API) serves both the @Threads UI and a search-conversations agent tool. The foundation tasks (migration, contracts, repository) feed into parallel consumer paths: the WS/client/composer path for user-facing @Threads mentions, the projector sync for keeping FTS in sync, and the agent tool for AI-facing search.
